attributes.body_ja:
「兼（か）ねる」はもともと「一（ひと）つで二（ふた）つ以上（いじょう）の役割（やくわり）を果（は）たすこと」を意味（いみ）する一段動詞（いちだんどうし）ですが、動詞（どうし）のマス形（けい）とくっつくと「(A) は不可能（ふかのう）だ」や「(A) をすることができない」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。この文型（ぶんけい）には、話（はな）し手（て）は本当（ほんとう）は (A) をしたいが、外的（がいてき）な理由（りゆう）（難（むずか）しい・忙（いそが）しい・ためらいがあるなど）によってそれができないというニュアンスがあります。

この文型（ぶんけい）はたいていひらがなで書（か）かれますが、漢字（かんじ）を使（つか）っても問題（もんだい）ありません。

「兼（か）ねる」はやや硬（かた）い表現（ひょうげん）です。特（とく）にフォーマルな場面（ばめん）で「できない」と言（い）うと強（つよ）すぎるとか、直接的（ちょくせつてき）だと感（かん）じられる場合（ばあい）に、その婉曲的（えんきょくてき）な表現（ひょうげん）として使（つか）われることがあります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「兼（か）ねる」の「一（ひと）つで二（ふた）つ以上（いじょう）の役割（やくわり）を果（は）たすこと」という意味（いみ）は「広（ひろ）げる」や「伸（の）ばす」というニュアンスにも通（つう）じています。(A) という行動（こうどう）が、話（はな）し手（て）が対応（たいおう）できる範囲（はんい）を超（こ）えて、広（ひろ）がってしまっている、伸（の）びてしまっているというようなイメージです。
attributes.body:
兼（か）ねる, a る-Verb meaning 'to spread across' (usually 2 different activities or thought processes), often follows the ます-stem of other verbs in order to highlight that '(A) is not possible'. However, 兼（か）ねる often indicates that the speaker would actually like to do (A), but cannot due to some external circumstances such as difficulty, already being busy, being hesitant, etc.

This particular grammar pattern will most frequently be seen in its non-kanji form, although both are possible.

兼（か）ねる is somewhat formal, and may be used in cases where a phrase like できない would be considered too strong, so the speaker wants to lightly imply that (A) cannot be done.

Fun-fact

As 兼（か）ねる means 'to spread across', this expression can be thought of as similar to 'to be a stretch' in English. It just indicates that doing the action of (A) would be a stretch of the speaker's ability or capacity.

Both 〜得ない and かねる express inability, but differ in nuance. 〜得ない indicates objective impossibility, as in あり得ない話 (an unthinkable or impossible story). かねる reflects personal or emotional hesitation, often used in polite refusals in business contexts, as in お答えできかねます (I’m unable to answer).

attributes.body: かねる and かねない are the same pattern in negative and positive forms. かねる implies being unable to do something, so its affirmative form carries a negative meaning, as in 分かりかねる (I cannot understand). かねない expresses a potential undesirable outcome, as in 誤解を招きかねない (It might invite misunderstanding). Both are formal/polite and often used in business contexts to soften assertions.

attributes.body: を兼ねて and かねる come from the same verb, but their uses differ. を兼ねて expresses that something serves two purposes simultaneously, as in 運動を兼ねて散歩してきた (I went for a walk, also to get some exercise). かねる attaches to verb stems to express inability politely or indirectly, as in 私には分かりかねます (I’m afraid I don’t understand).

attributes.body: Both express inability to do something, but differ in tone and usage. わけにはいかない follows the non-past form of a verb and implies a moral or social reason for being unable to act, e.g. 約束を破るわけにはいかない 'I can't break my promise.' かねる attaches to the verb stem and is more formal, often used in business settings for polite refusals or hesitations, e.g. 私には分かりかねます 'I'm afraid I'm not sure.'

attributes.body: Both 切れない and かねる express inability to do something, but differ in tone and nuance. 切れない describes physical or practical inability to complete an action, e.g. '食べ切れない' ('I can't finish eating it'). かねる conveys emotional or psychological reluctance and often appears in formal or polite refusals, e.g. '分かりかねます' ('I'm afraid I don't know').
